title: KV/prefix cache incident follow-up: poisoning + eviction leak hardening
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: On 2026-02-27 we observed a capacity event and progressive OOMs on a production serving pool. Root cause analysis points to a sequence where the prefix (KV) cache accepted malformed key ranges combined with a concurrent eviction path bug that caused stale pointers to remain reachable (memory leak) and occasional cache poisoning where one customer's prefix data was incorrectly reused for another request shape. This ticket tracks follow-ups, mitigation, and engineering action items from the postmortem.
incident_timeline:
2026-02-27 03:12 UTC: alert triggered for elevated memory on pool-us-east-1-gpu-3
2026-02-27 03:25 UTC: first OOM on node gpu-3-42 -> automatic node restart
2026-02-27 03:48 UTC: repeated OOMs across shard set; traffic shifted by smart-routing fallback
2026-02-27 04:10 UTC: emergency rollback to cache version v1.18 (disabled new prefix dedupe optimization)
2026-02-27 05:05 UTC: traffic stabilized; mitigations remain in place while RCA proceeds
root_cause: Two cooperating failures: (1) prefix-dedup optimization introduced a key-normalization path that could return an alias for overlapping prefixes without cloning ownership semantics; (2) eviction code had a race during concurrent compaction that could drop the in-cache reference count but not reclaim auxiliary allocation, leaving a memory leak. In certain race windows the aliasing allowed one request to observe another customer's prefix contents (cache poisoning).
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back prefix-dedup optimization (runtime v1.18 revert) across affected pools (done)
Temporarily reduced prefix cache size from 12GB to 6GB on dedicated pools to reduce OOM risk (done)
Enabled aggressive node-level restarts via orchestrator when per-shard memory > 85% for 60s (done)
Scoped smart-routing to avoid routing mixed-tenant noisy traffic to impacted pools (done)
long_term_actions: Add ownership semantics to prefix dedupe: ensure any alias returns an immutable view or a clone; implement copy-on-write for in-flight mutations — owner: Liam Chen, due 2026-03-18
Fix eviction race: convert eviction/compaction to be single-threaded per-shard or guarded by a lightweight epoch mechanism; include unit/integration tests — owner: Priya Kapoor, due 2026-03-15
Heap-safe invariants: add allocator auditing (valgrind-style) and periodic per-shard heap-scan in staging to detect leaks early — owner: Marcus Green, due 2026-03-22
Add blackbox fuzz tests for prefix overlap permutations and concurrent eviction scenarios; integrate into CI gate for runtime-compile jobs — owner: Nia Okoye, due 2026-03-29

Telemetry: emit per-prefix insertion counts, aliasing events, eviction latencies, and leak-suspect counters to Grafana; add alert when aliasing events > 0.1% of inserts for 5m — owner: SRE Team (oncall leads), due 2026-03-12 (telemetry baseline), 2026-03-20 (alerts)
API compatibility audit: validate that no customer-facing behavior changed by dedupe path; prepare migration notes for Dedicated/private customers — owner: Product Reliability, due 2026-03-25
Canary plan for reintroducing safe dedupe: staged canary across 1% -> 10% -> 50% traffic with failure rollback and memory guarding — owner: Release Engineering, due 2026-04-02
notes: We noticed the first poisoned-key reports came from a single high-throughput customer whose prefix cardinality was unusual (wide small prefixes). Reproduction in staging required aligning request shapes and concurrency windows.
SRE leveraged heap profiles from the pprof exporter to identify the growth site; this accelerated the fix. Keep pprof snapshots enabled for 48h after reintroducing dedupe in canary.
Action owners should comment progress on this Linear ticket and link PRs. For any schedule slips >48h, notify the incident lead (Ava Martinez) and update stakeholders.
Follow-up retrospective scheduled: 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC, attendees: runtime eng, SRE, product reliability, release eng, QA.
